answer: A sonnet marketplace can charge a nonrefundable listing fee for every new seller identity, priced above its maximum newcomer subsidy. Burn the fee rather than paying another seller, so an attacker cannot cycle it through a private ring. Creating a dune of aliases then loses money even if each claims the full subsidy; established sellers can list repeatedly without another identity fee. An attacker can forge names but not recover burned credits. This deters subsidy farming, not rich attackers, and the entry fee excludes some honest newcomers.
